A regular meeting of the Santa Monica City Council was called to order by Mayor Winterer at 5:32 p.m., on

ZONING  7.C. Introduction and First Reading of an Ordinance to Amend the
  Zoning Ordinance Making Changes, Corrections, and Clarifications to
  the Zoning Ordinance Related to Policy Issues That Have Arisen Since
  the Adoption of the Zoning Ordinance Through Its Implementation, was
  presented.

  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that the City Council introduce for first reading an
  ordinance amending the City’s Zoning Ordinance making changes,
  corrections, and clarifications to the Zoning Ordinance related to policy
  issues that have arisen since the adoption of the Zoning Ordinance through
  its implementation.

  Questions asked and answered of staff included: street wall height and why
  is a maximum needed and does the 11ft minimum change the number of
  stories a building can have; relating to Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs),
  what is the square footage limit; relating to ADUs, whether or not a “one size
  fits all” approach fits all lot sizes and instead it should be a percentage of lot
  size; relating to ADUs, why should the second floor be limited to 400 square
  feet; why does an ADU have to be subordinate; does state law on ADUs
  prescribe that the ADU be no larger than the primary building; can you have
  an ADU in an R-2 district; did staff receive feedback from the residents of
  Sunset Park regarding the notification postcards sent out by the city
  regarding the R-1 size; if the ADU size is raised to 1,200 under the Interim

  12  May 22, 2018
 Zoning Ordinance (IZO), then can people add 1,200 square feet onto their
property and not have it count towards the lot coverage calculations; since
enacting the IZO, what size ADUs are people looking for if they are not
looking for 1,200; would it be simple to have two ADU sizes; by definition
of state law, is there concern that the city would be discouraging ADUs if it
does not raise the ADUs above 650 square feet ; will the city bring the state
down on them if the ADU size is left at 650 square feet; what are the set-
backs for the 400 square feet second floor maximum ADUs; and, would
increasing the maximum ADU size from 800 square feet to 1,200 square feet,
exempting the first 160 square feet from the lot coverage and anything done
above and beyond that would count towards the lot coverage, re-open the
IZO.

Members of the public Denise Barton, Dave Rand, Zina Joseph, Nancy
Coleman, Nathaniel Wilson, Robert Poser, and Troy Fosler spoke on the
recommended action.

Considerable discussion ensued on topics including, but not limited to
Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) standards.

Motion by Mayor Pro Tem Davis, seconded by Mayor Winterer, to introduce
and hold first reading of the ordinance reading by title only and waiving
further reading thereof, making changes, corrections, and clarifications to the
Zoning Ordinance as proposed by staff with the exception that the maximum
size for Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) be reduced from 1,200 square
feet to 800 square feet.

Mayor Pro Tem Davis amended her motion, regarding ADUs, to make the
maximum ADU size be 650 square feet for lots that are 6,000 square feet or
less and 800 square feet for lots that are over 6,000 square feet, and to remove
the square footage limitation for the second story.

Chief Deputy City Attorney Yibin Shen clarified the motion by reading it
into the record as follows:

Amendment to Section 11 of the Zoning Ordinance, which is Section
9.31.300 of the Municipal Code, subsection F.2.b., Maximum Floor Area.
The total floor area of an Accessory Dwelling Unit up to 14 feet in height
shall not exceed 650 square feet for any lot up to 6,000 square feet or 800
square feet for any lot greater than 6,000 square feet. In addition, a parallel
change, the same language will be reflected in Section 9.31.300 of the
Municipal Code, subsection F.3.b., which impacts the second story ADUs.
Additionally, deletion of Section 9.31.300, f.3.b. Subsection i., no Accessory
Dwelling Unit or portion of an Accessory Dwelling Unit shall exceed 400
square feet on the second story.

  13  May 22, 2018
   The same reference to the 650 square feet also exists in the same Section
  9.31.300, but under B.1. Zoning Conformance Review, and under E.4.
  Conversion of an Existing House to an Accessory Dwelling Unit. The same
  reading will apply to these sections, as well.

  The motion was approved by the following vote:

  AYES:  Councilmembers O’Day, Himmelrich, Vazquez,
  Mayor Pro Tem Davis, Mayor Winterer
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Councilmembers McKeown ,O’Connor
